assumptions: ideal battery with no internal resistance
after an open-circuit disconnection the capacitor holds its charge

notes: Base: tau = 5 kOhm x 20 uF = 0.1 s; V = 12(1 - e^-0.8) = 12 x 0.550671 = 6.608 V. With 2 kOhm added in series: tau = 0.14 s, t/tau = 0.5714, e^-0.5714 = 0.56472, V = 12 x 0.43528 = 5.223 V. Disconnection at 50 ms (open circuit): V freezes at 12(1 - e^-0.5) = 4.722 V, assuming no leakage; this is relevant because 50 ms < 80 ms (it would be irrelevant if the disconnection came after 80 ms). T1DF2 'disconnected from the battery' must be read as opening the loop (not replacing the battery by a short, which would discharge the capacitor through R); T67B8's 'broken again' is slightly odd wording ('again' implies a prior break). The disconnected-resistor sentences (parts tray; spare board in a drawer) are D. Within each group the numbers and units match (2 kOhm; 50 ms).
